exclusion_reason: Implemented but red because FIX-004's full golden sequence needs the guest WndProc invoked as real code (the CPU core owns that; the manager falls back to DefWindowProc until then), plus the cursor, timer, browser user-gesture, and lost-focus-recovery path, none of which are wired, and no canvas-window/browser-input bridge is served. The USER32 window, message, and input slice exists generically in lib/user.mjs and its registration in lib/hle.mjs: the class registry and window lifecycle delivering the exact WM_NCCREATE/WM_CREATE and destroy sequence, the per-thread message queue exposed through GetMessageW, PeekMessageW, TranslateMessage (WM_KEYDOWN to WM_CHAR for a mapped key), and DispatchMessageW with the MSG struct marshaled to and from guest memory, SendMessageW/PostMessageW/PostQuitMessage, GetActiveWindow/GetFocus/IsWindow, the window geometry through GetClientRect/GetWindowRect/MoveWindow/AdjustWindowRect, and GetSystemMetrics over one declared virtual-desktop profile, plus the input translation that turns a key or pointer event into the exact WM_* posting.
promotion_trigger: Promote when FIX-004 reproduces the golden window, message, input, focus, cursor, and timer sequence.
expected_failing_assertion: The guest WndProc is not invoked as real code and the cursor, timer, and browser-gesture path are absent, so the full FIX-004 event trace cannot be reproduced.
active_gate_evidence: Two conformance suites carry a case for every served USER32 export (served user32 surface 14 to 23): the subsystem suite in test/user.test.mjs and the core-HLE suite; the message-order and create/destroy lifecycle fixtures replay identically across two runs, an input trace yields the exact WM_* sequence, and a dedicated test proves GetMessageW/GetClientRect/GetWindowRect/MoveWindow marshal the MSG and RECT structs through guest memory. The full suite stays green.
procedure: Drive a deterministic browser event script after explicit user-gesture setup.
Compare message order, coordinate, key state, focus, cursor, timer, and teardown artifact.
pass_criterion: The complete event trace matches the declared ordering and tolerance.
Reserved browser action and lost focus recover through documented behavior.
